turn_text: Welcome to Here2Lead, a podcast by the Congressional Hispanic Caucus Institute. I'm Marco Davis, CHI President and CEO, and I'm glad to have you join us today. Here2Lead features in-depth and inspiring conversations with community leaders on our nation's most pressing issues, recognizing Latino achievement, identity and culture, and sharing the impact of our work to advance Latino leadership. Today, I'm joined by Congressman Darren Soto, who represents Florida's 9th congressional district. Congressman Soto was born in Ringwood, New Jersey, and is the son of a Puerto Rican father and an Italian-American mother. He graduated from Rutgers University and George Washington University School of Law. After law school, he opened his own practice in Central Florida, where he practiced family law, civil litigation, and real estate law. Soto entered public service at the local level in 2006 and went on to be elected to the Florida House at the age of 29. He was later elected to the Florida Senate and then in 2016 became the first Floridian of Puerto Rican descent to serve in Congress. He currently serves on the House Committee on Energy and Commerce and the House Committee on Natural Resources. He is also the Chair of the Future Forum Caucus, a Vice Chair of the Congressional Hispanic Caucus, and a proud member of the New Democrat Coalition, Problem Solvers Caucus, Congressional Progressive Caucus, and LGBT Equality Caucus. And he is currently a member of the CHCI Board of Directors. Hey, Congressman, great to see you. Thanks for being here.
